headlines.title: Pittsburg PD officer shot by suspect who snuck gun into police station: report
headlines.description: The suspect accused of shooting a police officer inside the Pittsburg police station Thursday had snuck a gun into the station, according to the East Bay Times. Pittsburg police say an officer was booking a 31-year-old suspect on Thursday when the two got into an altercation and a gun was fired. Both men were hit. NBC Bay Area reached out to the police chief, asking how a gun made it into the booking area, but have not received a response. However, the East Bay Times reported the suspect somehow snuck the gun in. According to law enforcement analyst Michael Leininger, the typical protocol is that suspects are searching for weapons and officers secure their own firearms before entering the booking area. “When you take the handcuffs off an individual, they now have a certain amount of flexibility that they did not have, and if they want to take you on, you’ve enabled that by removing the handcuffs,” he said. The East Bay Times also reported the suspect then assaulted police and is now jailed on suspicion of attempted murder of a peace officer. Mayor Dionne Adams says she wants the investigation to play out. “I don’t know the protocols because I’m not an officer and I can’t really speak to what happened because I don’t know what happened and when, all I know is one of our officers is injured,” Adams said. So far, no update on the officer’s condition. As for the shooting, it remains under investigation by Pittsburg police and the Contra Costa County DA’s Office.

headlines.title: California gas prices surge ahead of Labor Day weekend
headlines.description: According to AAA, the average gas price in California for this Labor Day weekend is $5.81, $1.20 more expensive than a year ago. According to AAA, the average in California is climbing, right ahead of Labor Day weekend. Fuel prices are increasing as the war with Iran continues. “There’s no real sign of change in the war in the middle east and that is the main driver of the spike in gas prices, so I don’t think we’re likely to see any real relief in the next few weeks,” Energy Institute at Haas, UC Berkeley Faculty Director Severin Borenstein said. Borenstein says it’s difficult to predict what the price at the pump could look like in a few months too because so much of it is driven by the war. Jocelyn Moran has the full report in the video above.

headlines.title: Authorities respond to multiple medical calls during concert in San Jose
headlines.description: Emergency personnel responded to more than a dozen medical-related calls during the EDM concert at Discovery Meadow Friday night, San Jose police said. Police said around 10 people were taken to local hospitals for a variety of medical concerns, including suspected alcohol intoxication and drug-related issues.

headlines.title: Investigation underway after officer shot at Pittsburg police station
headlines.description: A police officer is recovering after getting shot inside a Pittsburg police station. The shooting occurred at the department’s booking room Thursday after what police are calling an altercation between an officer and a suspect when a gun was discharged, wounding both of them. Pittsburg police did not provide any further information about the incident on Friday, but policing experts said the shooting would not have happened if basic protocol had been followed. “There is one thing that is beyond dispute,” policing expert Michael Leininger said. “There was a significant mistake that was made.” Pittsburg Sep 3 Richmond Sep 3 Leininger said basic protocol to ensure a suspect is unarmed before bringing him inside a booking room, where fingerprints and phots are taken. Officers must also lock up their own weapons before entering. “When you take the handcuffs off an individual, they have a certain amount of flexibility that they did not have. And if they want to take you on, you’ve enabled them by removing the handcuffs,” Leininger said. “And you should not do that until you’re 100% certain that they do not have any weapons, and you yourself do not have any weapons.” NBC Bay Area reached out to the Pittsburg police chief specifically asking how a gun ended up in the booking room and who it belonged to, but did not receive a response Friday. Meanwhile, Mayor Dionne Adams is asking residents to pray for the officer, who is in serious condition. “All I know is one of our officers was injured,” Adams said. “And we’re continually praying to make sure he pulls through safely and he gets home to his family.” The mayor also said he could not share any new information on what led to the shooting, but assured the community a full investigation is underway. “I’m deeply saddened by what happened here and want to assure the community Pittsburg still remains a safe city,” Adams said. “I think the lesson here is that things happen. We want to make sure we know all the details before we come to conclusions.”

headlines.title: Emergency crews respond to hazardous materials incident in San Francisco
headlines.description: Emergency crews responded to a hazardous materials incident Friday in San Francisco. The San Francisco Fire Department said the incident involved muriatic acid and chlorine at the Presidio Golf and Concordia Golf Course. At least one person was taken to a hospital due to the incident. Hazardous materials units and fire crews responded to the scene to investigate. Residents and the public were asked to avoid the area. headlines.title: Court filings reveal new details in former Oakland Mayor Sheng Thao bribery case
headlines.description: Weeks ahead of the criminal trial for the corruption case involving former Oakland Mayor Sheng Thao, court filings from federal prosecutors reveal new details about the government’s case against Thao and other defendants. From transcripts of a private phone call to new revelations about Thao’s personal finances, the documents shed light on the alleged political hold the Duong family had on Thao and Oakland City Hall. The Duong’s own California Waste Solutions, Oakland’s recycling contractor. They also helped start a modular housing company called Evolutionary Homes. They’re both defendants in the criminal case, along with Thao and her longtime boyfriend Andre Jones. Included within the new court records is a transcript that prosecutors say comes from a recorded 2024 phone call between Andy Duong and an unnamed Oakland city council member. Early in the conversation, Duong invites the council member to join him on a yacht. “If you can roll then we can party up up in the yacht,” Duong allegedly said. According to the transcript, he also invited the council member to a future yacht event, saying, “I’ll keep you posted on another one…a private one for us only.” When the unnamed council member asks about the recall efforts against Thao, Duong responds, “…we put a stop to it.” Thao was eventually recalled later that year. In 2025, a grand jury delivered an eight-count indictment charging Thao, Jones and the Duongs with various bribery-related charges. Prosecutors say the Duongs helped Thao get elected and in exchange she allegedly used her position as mayor to get the city to buy housing units from the Duongs’ company, extend their recycling contract, and pay her boyfriend Andre Jones through a job with Evolutionary Homes. All four defendants have pleaded not guilty in the corruption case. According to the transcript of Duong’s alleged phone call with the council member, Duong appears to get frustrated about the city not buying housing units from Evolutionary Homes, yet, saying he called Sheng Thao and told her, “Aye, you got to get your [sh**] together…you want to – you know, you want to save your [mayoral] race…if you really want to continue for another term, then you better start acting right.” A separate filing from the government seems to show Thao and Jones were struggling to pay their energy, water and car loan bills. Prosecutors say that some of those alleged bribery payments helped pay rent on the couple’s shared house and that Thao benefited from any payments made to Jones. NBC Bay Area has reached out to the attorneys representing the Duongs, Jones and Thao. As of Friday evening, only Jones’ attorney has responded. He called the evidence the government is hoping to present, “incorrect, irrelevant, and unfairly prejudicial.” The criminal trial is scheduled to begin in October.
headlines.source: Candice Nguyen, Michael Bott and Alex Bozovic

headlines.title: Witnesses recount ‘chaotic' Richmond shooting and standoff
headlines.description: Some Richmond residents went through a tense situation during a two-hour standoff involving a woman, police and the Contra Costa County crisis team on Thursday. Police are investigating a neighborhood shooting and standoff that ended with one of their officers wounded. It started with a call reporting someone facing a mental health crisis. Authorities say the suspect was arrested and police said despite being shot at, they never fired back. Steven Foster, who witnessed the shooting, recorded it all from a nearby parking lot, posting the scary scene to his Instagram page. “I started to hear boom, boom, boom. Loud shots,” he said. “All I can say is that it was crazy. There was all kinds of shots, there was all kinds of chemicals. I walked in and I got some tear gas, I think in my eyes. It was hard to breathe.” A man who lives next door to the woman accused of shooting the officer says it all started around 6:45 p.m., just after a Contra Costa County Sheriff’s Office crisis negotiator called for back-up. One neighbor said he heard an explosion before the first shots were fired. “I’m not sure what that explosion was, but the gunshots were definitely loud and it sounded to me like it was a rifle,” Jason C. said. The two witnesses said they’re glad that the officer, a veteran of Richmond PD, will recover and that no one else was hurt. “Shout out to Richmond and shout out to everyone who was working on this. Glad to hear everyone was alright,” Foster said. “I believe one officer did get hurt. Hopefully, they’re okay. But it’s just an unfortunate thing, and I pray everybody is doing alright,” Jason C. said. Bullets hit the officer, a patrol car, neighbors’ cars and homes, but Richmond police officials say no officers ever fired a single shot even though the woman continued to shoot at them from inside the barricaded home. “Given the number of rounds fired, this incident could have ended with many additional injuries or several losses of life,” Richmond police Chief Tim Simmons said during a press conference Thursday night. Witnesses agree this could have ended with a lot more people hurt or worse. “I was concerned that somebody died, but fortunately nobody did,” Jason C. said. “If no one got seriously injured – that’s a good start. We’ll take it,” Foster said. A SWAT team arrested the woman when she exited the home, after police shot chemical cannisters through a window. The woman’s identity has not been released.

headlines.title: Police will not raise boat that capsized in San Francisco Bay
headlines.description: The San Francisco Police Department said Friday it will not raise the boat that capsized in San Francisco Bay in July. The decision comes two months after the boat named Volare capsized. Four of its 20 passengers died, including one who is presumed missing. Police are still working to understand what triggered the disaster, but they said they can do so without salvaging the boat. headlines.title: San Francisco's immigration court permanently closes, shifts cases to Concord
headlines.description: San Francisco immigration court, once one of the busiest immigration courts in the country, permanently closed Friday. Now immigration attorneys and their clients tell NBC Bay Area the move could exacerbate the court’s backlog of pending cases and potentially trigger more delays and confusion for immigrants navigating an already complicated process. The move will consolidate most of the over 115,000 pending cases under the Concord Immigration Court, which already had a backlog of nearly 59,000 cases, according to figures compiled by the Transactional Records Access Clearinghouse, or TRAC. The Concord court, about 30 miles away from the San Francisco court, opened in 2024 to help ease a national backlog of cases that threatened to overwhelm the immigration court system. San Francisco Jan 8 Investigative Unit Nov 25, 2025 San Francisco Nov 21, 2025 San Francisco’s immigration court had a nearly 71% grant rate for asylum and other relief, much higher than the 48% nationwide, according to TRAC data. The closure comes after a dramatic reduction in San Francisco’s immigration court bench. Before President Donald Trump took office in 2025, the court employed 21 judges. Only two remained at the city’s Sansome Street location this week. NBC Bay Area’s Investigative Unit found that the departures forced many cases to be reassigned or rescheduled— some years into the future. The court’s closing was first announced in January, when court personnel were told that the Department of Justice would not renew its lease at 100 Montgomery Street and that the courthouse was expected to close in January 2027. Employees were told they could begin relocating to Concord as early as the summer. But the justice department accelerated the timeline. The Montgomery Street location stopped holding hearings in May, although some administrative and filing operations continued during the transition. The Executive Office for Immigration Review, the justice department agency that oversees the nation’s immigration courts, announced that the San Francisco court would formally close at the end of the day on Friday, Sept. 4. The remaining courtrooms at 630 Sansome Street will become a hearing location under the administrative control of the Concord Immigration Court. EOIR said cases will be adjudicated either in Concord or remotely. When NBC Bay Area visited the Sansome Street location this week, the long lines that once wrapped around the building for immigration hearings and ICE check-ins were gone. Outside, NBC Bay Area met Daisy, a Honduran asylum seeker who said she came to the United States two years ago after fleeing violence in her country. “There are people like us who want to work honestly and do things right,” Daisy said in Spanish. “I help care for older adults, and I’m trying to pay my taxes—and not be a burden on this country.” The courthouse had also become a focal point of immigration enforcement after federal agents began arresting immigrants following scheduled court appearances. EOIR said it determined that relocating operations from Montgomery Street to Concord would be more cost-effective. The agency said it would issue new notices to everyone whose case is reassigned. But the closure has also drawn scrutiny from Congress. Rep. Mark DeSaulnier, who represents the district where the Concord court is located, sent EOIR a letter seeking information about the decision-making process, the effect on the region’s case backlog and whether the Concord court has the resources to absorb the transferred cases. “It’s just about what was the process? What was the rationale for doing it?” DeSaulnier told NBC Bay Area. “What kind of analysis did you do? Is it going to help with the backlog? All those things—and we haven’t had a response.”

headlines.title: Interest rates might not go down yet. Here's why
headlines.description: President Donald Trump said he’d like for interest rates to go down, but that’s a decision made by the Federal Reserve, which says it wants to see inflation at 2% before making cuts. When interest rates move, they generally take credit card rates, mortgage rates and even student loan rates with them. The Federal Reserve’s decision means prices are likely to remain high for now, largely because the economy is strong. Additionally, unemployment is low and the national job number is up. However, Bay Area tech companies, including PayPal and Uber, have been cutting jobs. Scott Budman has the full report in the video above.

headlines.title: Morgan Hill camp counselor held without bail after child molestation charges
headlines.description: A Gilroy man was officially charged Friday with molesting three 10-year girls while working as a summer camp counselor. The case also brought California’s bail debate back into the spotlight after victims came forward, one-by-one, leading Anthony Joseph Ramos to be arrested three times. Each time Ramos was arrested he was granted bail. The Santa Clara County District Attorney’s Office consolidated all three cases and pushed the court to hold the suspect without bail. Judge Stuart Scott agreed and said he was convinced Ramon was a potential danger to the community. Ramon was then put into handcuffs. Morgan Hill Sep 3 Morgan Hill Jul 17 Morgan Hill Jul 9 Ramon is accused of molesting three 10-year old girls at a summer camp field trip to the Morgan Hill Aquatic Center in June. He was charged Friday with three felony counts of lewd acts on a child under 14 with a “multiple victim” enhancement, which increases the possible sentences. But even after the judge agreed to hold Ramon without bail, the district attorney’s office said the case shows the flaws in the justice system. But Ramon’s attorney said his client followed all court orders and that his family sacrificed a lot to post bail. Prosecutors on Friday also revealed claims that child pornography was found on Ramon’s phone. His family declined to comment on the charges. For now, Ramon will remain in custody. His next court appearance will be held in about two weeks.

headlines.title: 8 arrested in San Jose shooting that killed a man, injured another
headlines.description: San Jose police Friday announced the arrests of eight people for their alleged involvement in a June shooting that killed a man and injured another. The suspects were arrested for their alleged parts in a shooting on June 28 near the intersection of North Market and West Santa Clara streets. One man, 24-year-old Anthony Contreras, died at the scene and another was taken to a hospital and listed in stable condition. The suspects were identified by police officials as Izaiah Hernandez, 18, Ezequiel Mercado, 20, Jaden Diaz-Mejia, 18, Fabian Diaz-Gomez, 18, and Johnny Picazo, 36, who were all booked into the Santa Clara County Main Jail on suspicion of murder, along with an unnamed 17-year-old suspect. Additionally, Sabastian Saldana, 34, and Nevaeh Luna-Rosales, 18, were booked into the Santa Clara County Main Jail on suspicion of crimes related to being accessories after the fact, according to police. The motive and circumstances surrounding the shooting are still under investigation. It was the city’s 13th homicide of 2026.
